observations: A correction to my round 7 note, which said the e2e evidence could only be taken after a code push. That is true of the `e2e` label alone: a `labeled` event is a pull-request event of the head commit, and a handoff head carrying `skip-checks: true` suppresses it. `gh workflow run e2e.yaml -R sjawhar/legion --ref legion/INFRA-567 -f script=<name>` is a `workflow_dispatch`, which that trailer does not suppress, and that is how run 40999737194 was taken at e719a7f2 — a handoff head. So one proof can be driven at any ref at any time, and only the five-at-once label run needs a code head.

The Go check's move onto the package is worth a reader's eye for what it does not do: it reads the config of the digest the package holds under the row's tag, which `crane copy` landed from the row's own upstream digest, so it still answers for the row's bytes; what it stops reading is Docker Hub. A row being copied is still read at its upstream first, which is the only moment bytes with a wrong label could land.
This round is a refactor plus two message changes; check-ci-images.sh's harness staying at 99 assertions while mirror-ci-images.sh's went 32 to 45 is the shape that fits it.
